title: Structural OCT Parameters Associated with Treatment Response and Macular Neovascularization Onset in Central Serous Chorioretinopathy.
summary: In a 96-eye, 36-month prospective CSC series, a decision-tree/logistic analysis associated OCT features and age with treatment response and MNV onset. The associations are cohort-specific and do not establish which treatment causes better outcomes.
ai_technology: a supervised decision-tree approach uses OCT measurements, hyperreflective foci, age and sex to associate imaging features with treatment response; logistic modeling analyzes MNV onset.
organization: Affiliation not stated in the reviewed material

evidence.tested: among 96 treatment-naive eyes followed for 36 months, OCT hyperreflective foci and age were associated with response to eplerenone/PDT; retinal/RPE/choroidal parameters were associated with MNV risk.
evidence.unknown: The result is tied to prospectively observed clinical/OCT/angiography outcomes through 36 months in one case series. No held-out or external model validation is reported; approval is limited to these cohort associations, not treatment-selection performance or causal benefit.
evidence.ai_role: a supervised decision-tree approach uses OCT measurements, hyperreflective foci, age and sex to associate imaging features with treatment response; logistic modeling analyzes MNV onset.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
